id: Re-Degradation Reveals Resolution | CVPR 2027 | addendum v3 | registered after run 2 and before run 3
scope: Frozen v1.0, addendum v2 and every rule registered so far stay exactly as they are, and the run-2 checkpoints are reused unchanged. Addendum v3 only adds three experiments (blocks B9-B11) and the rules below; it changes no earlier constant, step, threshold or estimator.
motivation: run 2: every win is on Gaussian heat blur, which matches the method's forward model
run 2: on real cross-dataset shifts the identified level is about 0 (no resolution change), so re-degradation has nothing to correct there
run 2: the real 25 -> 50 cm change costs only about 2 pp of accuracy, too little to separate estimators
run 2: classic no-reference blur metrics were not compared as identification baselines

corruptions.definition: ImageNet-C corruption functions and parameters (Hendrycks and Dietterich, ICLR 2019), re-implemented in numpy/scipy and checked in Cell 5.6; motion blur follows the numpy re-implementation of the ImageNet-C motion blur used by the imagecorruptions package; outputs are not JPEG re-encoded
corruptions.data: the ten evaluation datasets, seed 0, A2 and B each capped at 400 images (keyed subsample), the six method encoders
corruptions.estimators: the 11 baselines; the six plug-ins at the v1.0 and v2 levels; ATC@NR = ATC calibrated on A2 re-degraded to the level identified by the variance of the Laplacian (the most widely used classic no-reference blur metric, fixed in advance); known-corruption oracles = ATC, DoC, ATC-NE, PT, COT and COTT calibrated on A2 corrupted with the true family and severity (not label-free)

mvoi.data: SpaceNet MVOI (Atlanta, WorldView-2, one pass, 27 views from 7 to 54 degrees off-nadir, all resampled to a 0.5 m grid; public AWS bucket, no credentials); 48 tiles present in every view, 16 crops of 224 px per tile
mvoi.physics: source = nadir-7 crops of 32 tiles (A2 role), target = crops of the other 16 tiles in each of the 27 views (panchromatic band); identified level per view
mvoi.accuracy: building presence (footprint fraction >= 2% of the crop) from the public footprints; probe on nadir-7 crops of 16 tiles (A1), calibration on 16 other tiles (A2), targets = the 16 remaining tiles in 9 views (7 to 53 degrees); the six method encoders and every estimator of B9 except the oracles

metrics: variance of the Laplacian normalised by the image variance
spectral slope of the radially averaged power spectrum (log power vs log frequency, 0.05 <= lambda <= 2)
id_baselines.calibration: median metric of A2 re-degraded over CAL_GRID, inverted like CAL1 (label-free, encoder-free)
id_baselines.conditions: the seed-0 within-dataset conditions of B3 (recomputed bit-for-bit from the keyed streams)

C1.test: X@s_hat (v2 level) < X for the 6 plug-in pairs, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells (dataset x encoder x family x severity), Holm over the 6 pairs

C3.test: ATC_v2 < ATC, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells

C4.statistic: share of conditions (dataset x severity) whose v2 level is <= 0.5 px^2, and pooled |MAE(ATC_v2) - MAE(ATC)|

C5.status: EXCEEDED / MATCHED / BELOW from the hierarchical 95% CI of (ATC_v2 - strongest baseline of the group)

C6.comparison: pooled MAE of ATC_v2 minus the known-corruption oracle ATC, per family

V1.statistic: Spearman rho between the identified level and the off-nadir angle over the 26 off-nadir views

V2.control: nadir-7 target tiles against the nadir-7 source tiles

V3.test: ATC_v2 < ATC on the 8 off-nadir accuracy views x 6 encoders, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells

V4.comparison: ATC_v2 vs the strongest baseline on the off-nadir accuracy views

I1.comparison: median relative identification error of v1.0, the v2 level and every identification baseline, per regime (clean, noisy, label shift)

I2.test: noisy regime: relative error of the v2 level < that of the better no-reference metric, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired conditions
